The residence

Five rooms in a full-service complex

According to the broker, this is a spacious, bright five-room apartment on a high floor, in a quality Ramat Aviv complex with a swimming pool, a gym, a guard and other services. It comes with two parking spaces and a storage room.1

The rent, size, floor number and complex name were not published. Listings for five-room units other than penthouses, of 119 to 137 sqm in Ramat Aviv HaHadasha and Ramat Aviv Gimel, ask NIS 12,800 to 17,000 a month, and a 130 sqm top-floor unit in a building with a pool and gym asks NIS 18,000.2,3

Complex services such as a pool and a guard are priced into the building fee: in examples checked nearby, NIS 1,700 a month for 110 sqm in a building with a pool, gym and 24/7 security, and about NIS 2,300 for 138 sqm in a complex with a pool in north Tel Aviv.4,5

The location

Ramat Aviv: university, mall and museums

Ramat Aviv (Aleph) is bounded by Einstein Street to the north, Haim Levanon Street to the east and south and Namir Road to the west, while Neve Avivim, Ramat Aviv Gimel and Ramat Aviv HaHadasha count as its other parts.9 Ramat Aviv HaHadasha, between Propes and Einstein streets and between Levi Eshkol Boulevard and Namir Road, was built mainly from 1996 to 2016.7,10

The area holds Tel Aviv University's main campus of about 89 hectares, the Eretz Israel Museum, the Palmach Museum and ANU Museum of the Jewish People.9,11 Ramat Aviv Mall at 40 Einstein Street opened in 1997 with about 140 stores, and Ramat Aviv Gimel has two shopping centers, Shuster and Elram.8,12

The coastal park promenade, from Tel Baruch beach to Tzuk beach, opened in 2023.13 Car access relies mainly on Levi Eshkol Boulevard and Einstein Street, and the Einstein and Namir junction is congested at peak hours; the Green Line light rail is planned along Namir Road, Einstein Street and Haim Levanon Street.14,15

Transport

  • Green Line route in Ramat Aviv

    Planned along Namir Road, Einstein Street and Haim Levanon Street, with a sunken station at the Namir and Einstein junction. The works schedule was not verified.15

  • Planned stations nearby

    Station names include Tel Aviv University, Brodetsky and Namir. Order and exact locations not verified.25

  • Israel Railways, University station

    Operating. Walking distance depends on the address.26

  • Car access

    Via Levi Eshkol Boulevard and Einstein Street; the Einstein and Namir junction is congested at peak hours, per a 2025 report.14

  • Public transport to the city center

    About 25 to 30 minutes from Ramat Aviv HaHadasha and Plan Lamed, per a 2025 appraiser's estimate.14

Planning

What is planned nearby

Published plans and works, and what they may mean for a buyer or tenant. Based on published reports; not a substitute for a check with the planning authority.

  • Green Line works in Ramat Aviv15,23

    The southern section is expected in 2028 and the full line in 2030; until then, works along Namir Road, Einstein Street and Haim Levanon Street may affect traffic.

  • Nofei Yam North27

    191 vacant dunams between Nofei Yam and Propes Street. In March 2025 the permit freeze was extended by three years for re-planning, and heights could rise from 15 to 45 floors. Views toward the sea from high floors may change in the long term.

  • Sde Dov center plan28

    7,128 homes in towers of 20 and 45 floors. Objections were rejected in February 2025; the skyline to the west will change, and works will continue for years.

  • Barkai renewal compound, Ramat Aviv Gimel29

    370 homes. The design plan was approved on 29 October 2025; construction is expected inside Ramat Aviv Gimel.

Before you decide

What to check before signing

The questions a careful tenant asks about the unit and the complex, and the documents to obtain.

  • Which complex and building is it, and which floor out of how many?
  • What is the rent, what area appears on the arnona bill, and when is entry?
  • What is the va'ad bayit, and does it cover the pool, gym, guard and the other services, or are there separate fees?
  • Is the guard on duty 24/7, and is the pool heated, covered and open all year? What are the hours and the rules for tenants and guests?
  • Are the 2 parking spaces registered to the unit, and is EV charging available or allowed?
  • Is there a mamad in the apartment or a shelter on the floor?
  • What lease term, extension option and indexation are offered, which securities are required, and who pays the broker fee?
  • Is the apartment furnished, and what air conditioning and appliances are included?
  • Which schools is the address zoned for?
  • Is building work or Green Line work planned next to the complex during the lease?
  • The draft lease, including guarantees, indexation and option
  • A breakdown of the building fee and what it covers, and the pool and gym rules
  • The unit's latest arnona bill
  • Confirmation of the landlord's rights in the unit and both parking spaces
  • A handover record and equipment list

Questions and answers

Questions worth asking

What does the apartment cost per month?
The broker has not published a rent. Five-room units in Ramat Aviv HaHadasha and Ramat Aviv Gimel are offered at NIS 12,800 to 18,000 a month, and a building with a pool adds a building fee of about NIS 1,700 to 2,300, based on examples nearby.2,3
Which complex is it?
The complex name and address were not published; Meital Katzir gives them on direct contact. Per the broker, the complex has a swimming pool, a gym, a guard and further services.1
Does the Fair Rental Law apply?
It does if the rent does not exceed about NIS 20,000 a month, as across the whole asking range for similar units nearby. Guarantees are then capped at the lower of 3 months' rent or a third of the total rent.30,33
What is nearby?
Ramat Aviv has Tel Aviv University, Ramat Aviv Mall with about 140 stores, the Eretz Israel Museum and the Palmach Museum. Exact distances depend on the address.9,12
